newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak shares rise on unbundling details.
newsitem.headline: Malbak shares rise on unbundling details.

text.p: Shares in South African diversified industrial conglomerate, Malbak Ltd, rose on Tuesday following the release of further details on the group's intended unbundling.
Shares bucked the weaker trend on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange adding three percent to a morning high of 22.15 -- the share's best level in four months.
"The shares are up on the unbundling talk," a dealer said.
"Malbak said its net asset value is 24.60 rand, which is a premium over today's trade. Shares will move up to close this gap."

Malbak said on Monday its planned unbundling could add 15 percent in value for shareholders. They were likely to receive shares in the listed companies controlled by Malbak plus a cash payment for the unlisted entities.

Acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said Malbak's assets had been valued at 24.60 a share using Friday's closing prices and valuations for the unlisted companies. This was a 15.2 percent premium over Friday's closing price of 21.35 rand.
The target date for completion of the unbundling is the end of March 1997.
Better-than-expected annual results from Malbak, released on Monday, also helped the share's ascent, dealers said.
"The results were slightly better than we anticipated, but most of the (share's) rise is on the unbundling," a dealer said.
In the year to August 31, Malbak raised earnings before exeptional items 16 percent to 191 cents a share, beating a consensus forecast of between 181.3 and 184.0 cents a share.
Malbak's listed holdings are Foodcorp Ltd, Kohler Ltd, South African Druggists Ltd, Ellerine Ltd and New Clicks Ltd.
Unlisted subsidiaries include Malbak Motor Holdings, Defy, Eagle Freight, ICL (SA), Teledex and Amalgamated Appliances.
By 0950 GMT shares had slid off their best levels to trade at 21.95 rand after nearly 300,000 shares had changed hands valued at over 6.8 million rand.
